    The Morita equivalence of a full corner #

    For an idempotent e of a ring A, write C = eAe for the corner ring and eA for the right ideal, a left C-module. The functor

    Morita.functor e : Mod C ⥤ Mod A, M ↦ Hom_C(eA, M), (a φ)(x) = φ(x a)

    is fully faithful for every idempotent (full, faithful); when e is full, that is ∑ᵢ aᵢ e bᵢ = 1 for some aᵢ, bᵢ, it is essentially surjective (X ≅ Hom_C(eA, eX)) and hence an equivalence of categories (isEquivalence). This is the Morita equivalence used in the proof of Lemma 3.1.

    For a k-algebra A it is k-linear, preserves short exact sequences (preservesShortExact), and multiplies k-dimensions by at most the number of terms in ∑ aᵢ e bᵢ = 1 (rank_le, le_rank), so it preserves finite-dimensionality and the dimension of infinite-dimensional modules.

    The construction follows the right-module coinduction of LargeIndecomposable/Foundations/CornerRepFinite.lean and FullIdempotent.lean (multiplicative-bases-deformations, commit 7b9f39f221d8a420a1531f487a3b93ae6d26ce85), transposed to left modules.
